author: jsign
content:
uhm, i was checking the original [Reth optimization around this hint idea](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/stateless/blob/e3edc40a2dae527710d0ea18226384faff09a165/crates/stateless/src/recover_block.rs#L57-L78) but noticed they don't do the y-parity check I explained in the spec... so I think that was buggy.  Also see now that this code [was removed recently](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/stateless/pull/36), and they're back to full recovery.

So.. yeah, i think the current `zkvm_secp256k1_verify(..)` in the standards, we can't fully exploit this hint idea without including an extra precompile like `zkvm_secp256k1_verify_with_recovery_id(signing_hash, signature_rs, hinted_pubkey, recovery_id) -> bool` or similar.

But before proposing that prob it is worth double-checking again how much cost in mainnet blocks are for `zkvm_secp256k1_verify(..)` as is...
If we note that this is still a low % of cost, maybe this new precompile isn't worth it and we can remove `pub_keys` (woudn't oppose to that... hints in the input are a headache for the spec and testing 😅 )

author: jsign
content: Do you have handy the full zisk cost report for the cost you calcualte in PRs, and check how much comes from the tx signature verification? We can do some bigger dataset check anyway across different guests to conclude something eventually.

author: jsign
content:
uhm, I think everyone is using `zkvm_secp256k1_ecrecover`... feels to me `zkvm_secp256k1_verify(..)` as is today (without the recover_id check or returning) isn't quite useful. not sure why this was added to the accelerators originally, might have to dig a bit more.
(this msg doesn't change the fact that if sig verif as is with ecrecover acc is small % of total cost, we could remove the `zkevm_secp256k1_verify(..)` and `pub_keys` hint)

author: 0xrubo
content:
makes sense. i'd rather drop the hint than add a new primitive for it, and the numbers seem to agree.  a verify with a recovery id could only cut into the ~1.6% accelerator part, and a real verify isn't free, so the saving would be less than that. the signing hash is needed by every sound option, so that part stays either way. that's before counting the ~65 bytes of input per tx the hint adds.
on `zkvm_secp256k1_verify`: our guest only uses `zkvm_secp256k1_ecrecover`, so we don't depend on it. i'm not sure what it was originally added for either.
